comparisons.peer_topic: UK CMA Settlement on Fixed Income Products
comparisons.peer_summary: On February 21, 2025, the U.K. Competition and Markets Authority announced a settlement with the Firm regarding its activities concerning certain liquid fixed income products between 2009 and 2012.
comparisons.comparison: Both Citigroup (C) and Goldman Sachs (MS) disclosed specific settlements with the UK Competition and Markets Authority (CMA) concerning antitrust violations in government bond markets. Citi resolved a CMA investigation regarding unlawful information sharing on British pound sterling-denominated government bonds (gilts) for conduct between 2011 and 2013, resulting in a £17.16 million fine. Similarly, MS disclosed a settlement with the CMA regarding anti-competitive arrangements in liquid fixed income products, specifically covering its activities between 2009 and 2012. Both disclosures highlight regulatory enforcement in the UK sovereign debt market by the same authority during overlapping timeframes.

sentences.text: Regulatory Action: On May 24, 2023, the UK Competition and Markets Authority (CMA) announced that it had provisionally found that Citigroup, CGML, and four other banks unlawfully shared information related to the buying and selling of British pound sterling-denominated government bonds issued by the United Kingdom.
On February 21, 2025, the CMA announced resolutions with Citigroup and CGML related to conduct that occurred between 2011 and 2013 and imposed a fine of £17.16 million.

On February 21, 2025, the U.K. Competition and Markets Authority announced a settlement with the Firm, as well as other financial institutions, in connection with its investigation of suspected anti-competitive arrangements in the financial services sector, specifically regarding the Firm's activities concerning certain liquid fixed income products between 2009 and 2012.
